title: Columbus's third voyage, 1498–1500
summary: Six ships out of Sanlúcar; a southern run by Madeira and Cape Verde to the latitude of Trinidad, the first sight of South America at the Orinoco, then Hispaniola and the arrest of Columbus in chains.

events.label: Trinidad sighted, then the South American mainland
events.text: He sighted three hills and named the island for the Trinity. A few days later, in the Gulf of Paria, the great weight of fresh water from the Orinoco made him suspect a continent, and a land so green he wrote that it might be the Earthly Paradise.

events.label: Columbus arrested at Santo Domingo by Bobadilla
events.text: Francisco de Bobadilla, sent to look into complaints against the Columbus brothers' rule, had Columbus and his brothers put in irons and shipped to Spain. Columbus is said to have kept the shackles in his room and asked to be buried in them.

events.label: Columbus dies at Valladolid
events.text: He died in a rented house, ill, still arguing that the Crown owed him the titles and the tenth of the profits it had promised. He is generally said to have held that he had reached the edge of Asia. His bones were carried to Seville, then Santo Domingo, then Havana, then Seville again, and Seville and Santo Domingo both still claim him.
